method.SINGLE_BIDDER: Count of bids equals 1. CVC guidelines and GFR Rule 173 prefer competitive responses; a single bid is flagged for review without implying wrongdoing.
method.SHORT_WINDOW: GFR Rule 173 requires a minimum 21-day gap between NIT publication and bid submission for open tenders (where not exempted). Flagged when the gap is under 21 days.
method.PRICE_HIT_RATE: Winning bid >98% of the published estimated value. Not unusual in small tenders, but systematically high hit-rates across a buyer warrant review.
method.REPEAT_WINNER: Same winning vendor across multiple tenders from the same buyer in the last 24 months. Could indicate specialisation — flagged as an observation.
method.RETENDERED: Same scope/location retendered after an earlier cancellation. Normal after a no-bid event; flagged for discoverability.
method.RESTRICTIVE_TURNOVER: Required turnover exceeds the 85th percentile of comparable tenders in the same category. Can be legitimate for complex works; flagged for review.
method.DIRECT_NOMINATION: Awarded via nomination/single-source rather than open tender. Allowed under Rule 194 in specific cases but always flagged for transparency.

publish.title: Tender is published
publish.body: A government office posts the work, its rules and the last date on a procurement portal.

bid.title: Firms send bids
bid.body: Interested businesses sign up, pay the fee or EMD, and upload their bid before the deadline.

open.title: Bids are opened
open.body: The office opens the technical bids first, then the price bids of those who qualified.

award.title: Contract is awarded
award.body: Usually the lowest qualifying price wins, and the result is published.

build.title: Work gets done
build.body: The winner signs the contract, does the work and is paid in stages.
